extracted.intended_audience: established research leaders / principal investigators preparing ERC Advanced Grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit an ERC Advanced Grant proposal: eligibility, host arrangements, application contents and submission, evaluation on excellence, ethics review, and funding rules for long‑term, ground‑breaking research led by an established PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for the ERC Advanced Grants - called Principal Investigators (PI) - are expected to be active researchers who have a track-record of significant research achievements. The Principal Investigators should be exceptional leaders in terms of originality and significance of their research contributions. No specific eligibility criteria with respect to the academic requirements are foreseen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises leadership, originality and significant prior achievements rather than fixed academic titles or degrees; PI status is central to evaluation (PI and project are assessed in conjunction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field openness / bottom‑up approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be made in any field of research. The ERC's grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no thematic priorities — proposals in any scientific domain are eligible and assessed on their own merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution location and type requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted in a public or private research organisation (known as a Host Institution/HI). It could be the HI where the applicant already works, or any other HI located in one of the EU Member States or associated countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Host Institution must be located in an EU Member State or an associated country; the research must be physically carried out at an eligible HI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution responsibilities and PI‑HI relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution must offer suitable conditions for the PI to independently lead the research and manage funding. The PI can be hosted by any legal entity in an EU Member State or associated country. The PI does not need to be employed by the host institution at the time of proposal submission, but a mutual agreement and commitment are necessary if the proposal is successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single PI submits on behalf of the HI; the HI must commit to provide the conditions for independent leadership and funding management if the proposal is funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Principal Investigator submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an ERC grant require a single Principal Investigator (PI) to submit the application on behalf of their host institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scheme is centred on an individual PI-led project (not a consortium lead). Ensure the PI is clearly designated and authorised to submit for the HI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants support projects carried out by an individual researcher who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members. It is also possible to have one or more team members located in a non-European country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams may be internationally composed; vacancies can be published on Euraxess-Jobs; implementing arrangements exist to host non-European scientists under certain initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts, duration and special additional funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grants may be awarded up to €2.5 million for a period of 5 years (pro rata for projects of shorter duration). However, an additional €1 million can be made available to cover eligible “start‑up” costs for researchers moving from a third country to the EU or an associated country and/or the purchase of major equipment and/or access to large facilities and/or other major experimental and field work costs. To further encourage submissions by PIs currently based in non‑associated third countries, the ERC has decided to double the amount of additional funding that can be awarded to Advanced Grant applicants moving to the EU or an associated country to take up their ERC grant. In this case, the maximum additional funding shall be €2 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budgets within the specified caps and consider eligibility for additional start‑up or major equipment funding, especially if relocating from a third country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible costs coverage and lump sum implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of the total eligible direct costs of the research plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs. Advanced Grants will be implemented as a pilot call using a lump sum contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the pilot lump‑sum funding approach for Advanced Grants and consult the Q&A on lump sums and related guidance (personnel costs data, webinars, slides) for how costs will be treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents. The completed proposal needs to be submitted by the specified closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the call documents carefully to confirm required attachments and templates; incomplete applications may be rejected at the eligibility check stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process, versioning and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grant applications can only be submitted in response to a Call for Proposals. Calls are published on this page, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and in the Official Journal of the European Union. You can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by simply submitting a new version, which will overwrite the old one. You will get an ‘acknowledgement of receipt’ by e-mail for each submission. Submit your proposal as early as possible. Deadlines cannot be changed under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarise yourself with the EU submission service; allow time for internal reviews and revisions; use the acknowledgement as proof of submission; do not rely on deadline extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility check after deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: After the deadline: The ERC will check whether your proposal meets the call’s eligibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only proposals that meet eligibility proceed to external peer evaluation; ensure administrative and eligibility conditions are satisfied prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation principle: excellence as the sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who assess them on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion. It will be applied to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the proposal to demonstrate excellence of both the project idea and the PI's capability; non‑scientific factors or strategic priorities are not evaluation criteria — excellence governs selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality threshold, scoring and ranking (budgetary cut‑off)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are in charge of assessing and scoring the proposals. Those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut‑off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that passing reviewers' threshold does not guarantee funding; relative ranking and available budget determine which proposals are funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation panels, domain structure and use of remote referees
rubrics_metrics.description: For each call there are 28 panels, each covering a sub‑section of one of three domains: Life Sciences (LS), Physical and Engineering Sciences (PE), Social Sciences and Humanities (SH). Each ERC panel consists of a chairman and 10‑16 members. The panel chair and the panel members are selected by the ERC Scientific Council on the basis of their scientific reputation. In addition to the panel members (who act as 'generalists'), the ERC evaluations rely on input from remote experts external to the panel, called referees. They are scientists and scholars who bring in the necessary specialised expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel composition balances generalist panel members with specialist referees; panel chairs are published before the deadline and panel members' names are published after evaluation concludes. Consider which panel/subpanel best fits your proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review legal requirement and basis in application
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal that is selected for funding must undergo an ethics review. This is a legal requirement under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme - Regulation 2021/695: Eligible actions and ethical principles (Article 18) and Ethics (Article 19). The basis for this ethics review is Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table – EIT – and the Ethics Self‑Assessment – ESA) and Part B of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a well‑detailed Ethics Self‑Assessment (ESA) and complete the Ethics Issues Table in Part A to facilitate the ethics review and avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review stages, timelines and possible follow‑up
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethics review comprises 3 stages: Ethics pre‑screening (performed internally by ERCEA staff to clear proposals without ethics issues or with simple ethics issues); Ethics screening (panels of independent ethics reviewers identify proposals with potentially Serious and/or Complex ethics issues; clearance of proposals with non‑Serious and/or Complex ethics issues can include observations and references to documents to be kept on file and provided to ERCEA, upon request only; applicants might be contacted to provide additional information on the ethics handling of their proposals — typically one week after the screening panel and applicants are given 3 weeks to reply); Ethics assessment (panels of independent ethics reviewers discuss the Serious and/or Complex ethics issues of the proposals; in case follow‑up is needed during project implementation, ethics deliverables might be formulated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate possible contacts for additional information shortly after screening and prepare clear, documented ethics handling plans; serious/complex issues may require ethics deliverables during implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific ethics requirement for hESC research
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that research proposals involving the use of hESCs will need to undergo all of the steps of the Ethics review and also a specific EC approval following a consultation to the HE programme committee comitology procedure, as this is a legal requirement under HE framework programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your project involves human embryonic stem cells, prepare for additional mandatory approvals beyond the standard ethics review and allow time for the comitology consultation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant support, guidance documents and training resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the call is published: Find out which ERC grant and which call is suitable for you. Identify the Host Institution and team members you would like to work with. Contact the National Contact Point (NCP) in your country for support. Once the call is open: Read the call documents carefully. Contact the Host Institution and gather all the details you need for the application. Start writing your proposal. Allow time for other people to review your draft. Your NCP, peers and other scientists can all give you helpful support and feedback. Familiarise yourself with the EU submission service. Watch instructional videos describing the full ERC grant application and evaluation process, webinars and slides. Consult key documents such as the ERC Work Programme, Guide for Peer Reviewers, Gender Equality Plans, bias awareness guidance, and Q&A on lump sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NCPs, peer reviews, webinars and the provided documents to prepare a compliant, competitive submission; allow time for internal review and administrative checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and data tools for applicants and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Searching for data on ERC funded projects and proposals? You can use two different platforms for views and analysis of ERC funded projects and evaluated proposals: ERC dashboard (filter by funding scheme, country, year, panel, export data) and ERC Research Information System (ERIS) (rich filters, text mining, dynamic visualizations, project outputs & bibliometrics, export data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the dashboard and ERIS to explore examples of funded projects, panel behaviour, and bibliometric outputs to inform proposal design and positioning.
